chunks: Sama'ah asked him about food, dates, and raisins, and he said:
Nothing of these is valid to be exchanged as two for one, unless you exchange it from one type to another type. Then when you exchange it, there is no harm in it being two for one or more than that.

key_terms.اثْنَانِ بِوَاحِدٍ: an exchange ratio of two for one
key_terms.التَّمْرِ: dates, one of the ribawi items mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الزَّبِيبِ: raisins, another commodity mentioned in the exchange ruling
key_terms.الطَّعَامِ: food commodity subject to the ruling discussed here
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: is not valid or permissible in this legal context
key_terms.نَوْعٍ: a type or category of commodity

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to exchange dates or raisins in unequal amounts?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ribawi food items such as foodstuffs, dates, and raisins. It states that unequal exchange within the same type is not valid, but if the exchange is between different types, then disparity in amount is permitted.
